# Bound subprocess-heavy scripts/ tests

**Goal:** Stop the subprocess-spawning `scripts/` tests from serialising the
suite: `build-audio.test.ts` (20 spawn sites), `capture-gameplay.test.ts` (7),
`audio-balance-guard.test.ts` (7), `setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` (4)
and `recording-cli.test.ts` (4) each fork real Node/CLI processes. Bound them
with a measured change — smaller fixtures, a dedicated project/group, or a
stub where the subprocess boundary is not the behaviour under test — without
losing the coverage they provide (parent Desired change 6, producer confirmed
in-scope on 2026-10-19).

**Deliverables**

- Measurement of the current `scripts/` cost (per-file wall clock + process
  count) on an idle host, recorded with load.
- The chosen bounding mechanism (documented, measured): e.g. a separate Vitest
  project/group with capped concurrency, fixture trimming (smaller inputs,
  shorter durations, `--no-render` style flags), or a process-boundary double
  where the spawned process itself is already covered by another test.
- Proof that no subprocess-boundary behaviour lost its coverage: each stub or
  fixture reduction names the test that still exercises the real boundary (or
  a justification that the boundary is covered by a script's own test).
- Full suite green with the same test count.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`,
  `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts`,
  `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts`, `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`
- `./vitest.config.ts` (project/group + concurrency, if that is the chosen lever)
- `scripts/audio-fixtures.json` and similar fixture files touched by the bounding change

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The `scripts/` test group's contribution to full-suite wall clock is
  measured before and after on an idle host, with both figures and load recorded
  on this item.
- **AC2:** The change reduces the `scripts/` group cost measurably (target:
  no longer the longest serialisation point) with the full suite green and the
  same test count — no test deleted, skipped or `expected fail`-converted.
- **AC3:** Every removed or reduced real-subprocess exercise names the test that
  still covers that boundary (or records a justification), so no behavioural
  coverage is silently lost.
- **AC4:** The chosen mechanism is documented (config comment + work-item
  comment) with the measurement that justified it; if the measured change turns
  out large, the remainder is split into a linked child item rather than
  absorbed (producer's condition from intake).

**Dependencies:** blocked by the project split (C3) so the `scripts/` group can
be measured/grouped within the new project layout.

**References:** Parent AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV § Desired change 6, Constraint
"keep the change surgical"; producer answer 2026-10-19 (stay in scope).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts > SSR config hydration (evaluate.mjs path) > serves CSV-backed enemy/ship/difficulty values under Vite SSR
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
FAIL src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts > SSR config hydration (evaluate.mjs path) > serves CSV-backed enemy/ship/difficulty values under Vite SSR
Error: Test timed out in 30000ms.
Test Files 1 failed | 269 passed (270)
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `npx vitest run src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts` — or, for agents, via the test skill (`/skill:test`) as required by the test-execution policy.
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Prior Art & Recurrence

This is a **recurrence at a higher timeout ceiling**, not the original flake:

- AH-0MV8I2OCA009M9C1 ("[test-failure] balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts > serves CSV-backed enemy/ship/difficulty values under Vite SSR", completed, shipped in v0.1.13) addressed the *5 s* variant by adding `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30000 })` to the test file (commit `5b519480`), on the diagnosis of load-induced module-graph boot time.
- The test now times out at the **30 000 ms** ceiling, so raising the timeout again is unlikely to be a durable fix; the root cause (e.g. an unbounded/hanging Vite SSR boot, module-graph import, or dev-server middleware) needs to be identified before choosing a remediation.
- Related but not blocking: AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV (reduce full test-suite wall clock — per-test boots/sleeps) and AH-0MUIPP1UU000UT88 (same load-timeout class in the Phaser suite).

Duplicate check performed — no completed item fully satisfies the acceptance criteria below (the prior item fixed only the 5 s variant).

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts` — the failing test (boots a real Vite dev server via `createServer` + `ssrLoadModule`).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `loadConfigs()` SSR/bundled-CSV fallback path exercised by the test.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — dev-server `/api/csv/...` middleware that cannot resolve under SSR.
- `vitest.config.ts` — suite configuration (pool/threads/timeouts) affecting full-suite parallel load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ssr.test.ts > SSR config hydration (evaluate.mjs path) > serves CSV-backed enemy/ship/difficulty values under Vite SSR` passes when run against the latest `dev` — including in a full-suite parallel run (the failure is load-induced, so an isolated pass alone does not satisfy this AC).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — at minimum a root-cause/fix note on this work item, plus any now-inaccurate timeout/flakiness comment in the test file or `docs/dev`.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill, per the test-execution policy).

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once (full suite and isolated), capturing whether the boot or the assertions is where time is spent.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.
4. Compare against the prior 5 s fix (AH-0MV8I2OCA009M9C1): establish whether the 30 s ceiling is still simply too low under load or whether the SSR boot has begun hanging, before deciding between a timeout/config change and a structural fix.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Prior fix: AH-0MV8I2OCA009M9C1 (commit `5b519480`)
- Related: AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, AH-0MUIPP1UU000UT88
- CI artifacts: (not available)

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6VVDP003L39A** (sibling under the epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Context

AH-0MVF6VVDP003L39A removed wall-clock waits from the heaviest / most flake-prone suites (PlayScene + CombatScene.equivalence + GymPowerUpsUtility + GymFormationScene) — 34 sites in 4 files — and added:
- `advanceGame(game, ms)` in `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — fixed-delta `game.step` simulated time, loop state preserved, no sleeping;
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — a code-only scan that fails when a `setTimeout` wait appears outside a documented, **self-pruning** allow-list, plus behavioural tests for `advanceGame`.

The remaining files are listed in that guard's `ALLOW_LIST` (28 entries, each 'pending migration'). This item migrates them, shrinking the list to empty.

## Remaining files (wait counts at hand-off, 2026-10-19)

| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` | 32 |
| `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` | 29 |
| `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts` | 14 |
| `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` | 14 |
| `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` | 11 |
| `src/scenes/TelemetryConsentScene.test.ts` | 4 |
| `src/entities/Player.test.ts` | 4 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts` | 2 each |
| `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`, `LeaderboardScene.test.ts` | 2 each |
| `src/scenes/gym/{GymWeaponLeveling,GymPowerUpLeveling,GymPlayer,GymMinerals,GymLevel,GymCurveSequencer,GymBotTuning}.test.ts` | 1 each |
| `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts`, `src/scenes/{demoMode.integration,demoBaselineDiscriminating,RebindableControls,PlayScenePause,PauseSettingsIntegration,PauseScene,HelpScene}.test.ts`, `src/core/Game.test.ts` | 1 each |

## Approach

1. For each file, replace the wait helper (`await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, N))`, a local `settle`/`tick`/`sleep` helper, or `await wait(N)`) with `await advanceGame(<scene>.game, N)`. Where the wait existed to reach a *condition* (a transition, a scene start), prefer `stepGameUntil(game, label, predicate)`.
2. Migrate in batches that keep the tree green (build → test → commit per batch), heaviest files first (GameOverScene, MenuScene, SettingsScene, MineralChoiceScene, GymIndex).
3. Delete each migrated file's entry from `ALLOW_LIST` in `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — the guard fails on stale entries, so the list must shrink to empty.
4. If any site genuinely must wait on real external async work (e.g. a telemetry flush that is not game-frame driven), record it as a documented allow-list entry with the reason and a linked item; do not invent a fake replacement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** All 28 files are migrated (or a genuinely-non-game wait is documented in the allow-list with a reason), and `ALLOW_LIST` in `wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` is empty at the end.
- **AC2:** The full suite is green with the same test count after each batch; no test deleted, skipped or `expected fail`-converted.
- **AC3:** Repeatable full suite (≥ 2 consecutive runs) with no new load-sensitive flake items filed.
- **AC4:** `advanceGame`/`stepGameUntil` remain covered by the guard's behavioural tests, and the guard still passes on the migrated tree.

## References

- AH-0MVF6VVDP003L39A (in_review) — the batch-1 migration, the helper and the guard.
- `README.md` § Testing conventions — the replacement idiom documented there.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ** (epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Problem

The `scripts/` test group costs ~184 s at load 32, and **140 s of that is one test**: `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` → *integration — real ffmpeg compile of synthetic footage (AC6)*. It runs the production compile end to end (960×540@60 VP9 re-encode of the promo/showreel/highlight deliverables plus brightness validation via ffprobe).

Measured in AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ:
- Fixture trimming (320×180@30, `-cpu-used 8`, ~18× fewer setup pixel-frames) gave **no measurable wall-clock change** (A/B back-to-back at load ~30: 140.9 s vs 140.4 s) — the setup encode is not the bottleneck.
- The cost is the production encoder settings themselves (deliberate: they are what the deliverable ACs require).

## Why this needs a producer decision

The only remaining levers change what the *audit-accepted full suite* covers:

1. Move the real-ffmpeg smoke into a separate project/type (e.g. `--type e2e` or a `release` project) excluded from the default `npm test`/`--type full` run — the full-suite test count drops by 1 and the audit evidence no longer covers the real encoder path.
2. Keep it in the full suite (status quo) and accept ~140 s as a floor that runs in parallel with the rest of the suite.
3. Reduce the production deliverable settings for all encodes (not acceptable — they are product requirements).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Producer records a decision (keep in the default full suite / move to a gated type / other) with the rationale.
- **AC2:** If moved: the gated type is registered via `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, the audit contract is explicitly re-stated (which type is audit-accepted full-suite evidence), and `--type full` still passes with the documented test count.
- **AC3:** If kept: `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` records the ~140 s floor as an expected, parallelisable cost so future timing work does not chase it.

## References

- AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ — measurements, the bounded fixtures and the A/B result.
- AH-0MVF6W8NC006RT2B (C9) — final timing validation; needs this decision to state the full-suite floor honestly.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP** (requested by the producer, 2026-10-19; epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Request

'Consider deleting tests that build audio' — evaluate whether the audio build/guard test suites should be deleted rather than bounded, given they are subprocess-heavy (they shell out to the ToneForge/audio pipeline) and their subject may already be enforced elsewhere (CI build, `npm run build-audio:verify`, `npm run build`).

## Current facts (measured 2026-10-19, load ~28, 16 cpus)

- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — **39.3 s**, 42 tests, 20 real subprocess spawn sites.
- `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` — **1.2 s**, 31 tests, 7 spawn sites (cheap; deletion unlikely to be justified on time alone).
- By contrast `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`'s real-ffmpeg smoke was the group's 140 s floor and is being moved to a gated `e2e` type (AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP).
- `npm run build` already runs `build-audio.sh` and `npm run check-bundle`; `npm run build-audio:verify` runs `scripts/build-audio.sh --verify && node scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` — so **both** suites' subjects are reachable outside the test run.

## Decision to make

For each suite, one of:
1. **Delete** — its invariants are fully enforced by the build/verify scripts (then say which script, and confirm the script runs in CI/release).
2. **Move to the gated `e2e` type** (the mechanism built in AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP) — keeps the coverage available on demand without costing the full suite.
3. **Keep in the full suite** — only if the tests assert something the build scripts do not (e.g. hermetic fixture behaviour, error paths, balance invariants not checked by `audio-balance-guard.mjs`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Each suite's assertions are mapped to the production script/CI step that would catch the same regression, or the gap is identified (`build-audio.test.ts` 42 tests, `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` 31 tests enumerated).
- **AC2:** A per-suite decision (delete / move to `e2e` / keep) is recorded with evidence, plus the resulting change to `scripts/` wall clock (before/after measured, load recorded).
- **AC3:** No invariant is silently lost: anything deleted has a named replacement check that runs in the release pipeline (`npm run build`, `npm run build-audio:verify`) or a linked item to add one.
- **AC4:** Full suite green with the documented test count; the audit contract (`--type full`) is re-stated if the count changes.

## References

- AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP — the `e2e` gated-type mechanism this can reuse.
- AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ — the subprocess measurements that identified `scripts/` costs.
- `package.json` scripts `build`, `build-audio`, `build-audio:verify`.

data.comment:
## Measurements, the bound applied, and the honest verdict (AC1-AC4)

### Before (idle-ish host, load 27-32)
`npx vitest run scripts/` → **16 files, 494 tests, 184 s** (tests phase 232 s). Per-file (JSON reporter):

| File | Time | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` | **163.2 s** | 110 |
| `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` | 39.3 s | 42 |
| `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` | 6.2 s | 19 |
| `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` | 4.2 s | 187 |
| `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` | 1.4 s | 8 |
| `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` | 1.2 s | 31 |
| other 10 files | < 1.5 s each | — |

The inventory in the description was stale: **`compile-promo.test.ts` (163 s) is the group's serialisation point**, not the five files listed. Within it, one test dominates: *integration — real ffmpeg compile of synthetic footage (AC6)* at **109.5 s** (all other 109 tests total ~0.4 s), and its `beforeAll` fixture encode adds ~53 s.

### Bound applied
Fixture trimming for the synthetic colour pattern: `testsrc2=960x540@60` → `320x180@30`, `-deadline realtime -cpu-used 8` — **~18× fewer pixel-frames** in setup. No production setting touched; the compile path and its 960×540@60 VP9 deliverables are still exercised end-to-end.

### After — measured A/B, back-to-back at load ~30 (same host, same hour)
| Variant | `compile-promo.test.ts` wall clock |
|---|---|
| original fixtures | 140.92 s |
| bounded fixtures | 140.37 s |

**Verdict: no measurable change (≈0.4 %).** The fixture setup is *not* the bottleneck — the dominant cost is the production VP9 deliverable re-encode (promo + showreel + highlights) plus brightness validation via ffprobe, which is exactly what the deliverable ACs require. The bound is kept because it is a strict reduction in work with identical coverage, but it is **not claimed as a wall-clock win**.

### AC assessment
- **AC1 met** — before/after measurements with per-file breakdown and load recorded above.
- **AC2 NOT met** — no measurable reduction: the `scripts/` group remains bounded by one legitimate real-ffmpeg encode test. Per the item's rule ('if the saving is small… record the negative result — no speculative change'), no configuration change is shipped.
- **AC3 met** — no subprocess-boundary coverage was reduced: the real ffmpeg compile, probe and validation still run (only the synthetic *source* encode shrank); `build-audio`/`recording-cli`/`capture-gameplay` are untouched.
- **AC4 met** — the measurement and its verdict are documented next to the change and here. The remaining lever (moving the real-ffmpeg smoke out of the default full suite) changes the audit contract, so it is split to **AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP** for a producer decision rather than absorbed.

**Validation:** full suite green at the committed state — 275 files, 6044 passed + 23 expected fail (6067), exit 0 (533 s at load ~23-27).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Producer direction (2026-10-19, interactive): the AC3 strategic decision is DEFERRED TO THIS ITEM.**

Context: the epic's AC3 (*full suite ≤ 50 % of the 314 s median baseline, i.e. ~150 s*) had two intended levers — AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG (Phaser transform dedupe, **measured negative, rejected**) and this item (per-describe boot reuse). C7 is therefore the last realistic lever.

Direction recorded:

- Do **not** decide AC3's fate outside this item. Run the measurement (AC1) and the adopt-or-reject evaluation (AC2-AC4) first.
- If C7 delivers a material saving → adopt per-suite where the reset is provably safe and record the achieved full-suite number (2 consecutive runs, load recorded), then return to the epic with the measured result.
- If C7 is **negative or only partial** → record that outcome here (AC4) *and* write up, on this item, the two options for the producer:
  - **(a)** relax/redefine the epic's AC3 with a documented rationale (e.g. the win is the 43.5 s `unit` loop + zero boot sleeps + repeatable green runs rather than halving the full suite), or
  - **(b)** authorise moving heavy real-binary work out of the audit-accepted full suite — the same class of change already approved for the real-ffmpeg promo smoke in **AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP** (gated `e2e` type).
  Present both with the measured cost/coverage trade-off; do not pick one unilaterally.
- Validation caveat: AC3 of this item needs **2 consecutive full runs on a quiet host**. Do not attempt to certify stability while the host is under other agents' load (observed load 3-40 during the C1-C6 work); record the load with every run.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Producer decision (2026-10-19, interactive): remove the real-ffmpeg promo smoke test from the default full suite.**

Interpretation applied (confirm if wrong): the smoke is **taken out of the audit-accepted `--type full`/`npm test` run** — not deleted — so its real-encoder coverage stays available on demand via a gated test type. Concretely that means:

1. Move the single `it` + its `beforeAll`/`afterAll` fixtures out of `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` (which keeps its other **111** pure/injected-subprocess tests, including `ffmpeg driver — compile orchestration with injected subprocesses (AC6)`) into `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`.
2. Exclude `*.e2e.test.ts` from the `unit`/`integration` project selection (so `--type full` no longer runs it) and add a third Vitest project `e2e` for it.
3. Register `{"types": {"e2e": ["npx vitest run --project e2e"]}}` in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` so the smoke is one sanctioned command (`/skill:test --type e2e`) and remains wired into release verification.
4. Re-state the audit contract in the docs: `--type full` is the only audit-accepted full-suite evidence; `e2e` has an independent cache key.

Expected effect: the full suite drops **1 test** (6067 → 6066) and `scripts/` loses its ~140 s floor; the remaining `scripts/` cost is ~20-40 s (build-audio 39 s at load 28).

Coverage retained rather than lost: the pure command-building / probe / brightness / validation-verdict / orchestration-with-injected-subprocesses suites (111 tests) continue to run in the default suite; the gated `e2e` run exercises the real encoder contract (vp9 960×540 + opus, non-trivial brightness, probe-able durations).

**Implementation requires an explicit implement invocation** (per the repo rule that code is only written under `/skill:implement <id>`): `/skill:implement AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP`.

If 'remove' meant **delete the test entirely** (no gated type), say so and I will amend this decision before implementing — that would permanently drop the real-encoder coverage.
